'''Eamonn Anthony O'Brien''' {{postnominals|country=NZL|FRSNZ}} is a professor of [[mathematics]] at the [[University of Auckland]], New Zealand, known for his work in [[computational group theory]] and [[p-group|{{mvar|p}}-groups]].

==Education==
O'Brien obtained his B.Sc. (Hons) from the [[NUI Galway|National University of Ireland (Galway)]] in 1983. 
He completed his [[Ph.D.]] in 1988 at the [[Australian National University]]. His dissertation, ''The Groups of Order Dividing 256'', was supervised by [[Michael F. Newman]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=57234}}</ref>

==Research==
O'Brien's early work concerned classification, up to isomorphism, of groups of order 256.<ref>{{citation
 | last = O'Brien | first = E. A.
 | doi = 10.1016/0021-8693(91)90261-6
 | issue = 1
 | journal = Journal of Algebra
 | mr = 1128656
 | pages = 219–235
 | title = The groups of order 256
 | volume = 143
 | year = 1991| doi-access = free
 }}</ref>  He developed early computer software to complete the classification, and to verify that the classification can correct errors in earlier counting.  This led to classifications of many further families of small order groups.  In 2000, together with Bettina Eick and Hans Ulrich Besche, O'Brien classified all groups of order at most 2000, excluding those of order 1024.  The groups of order 1024 were instead enumerated.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Besche | first1 = Hans Ulrich
 | last2 = Eick | first2 = Bettina
 | last3 = O'Brien | first3 = E. A.
 | doi = 10.1142/S0218196702001115
 | issue = 5
 | journal = International Journal of Algebra and Computation
 | mr = 1935567
 | pages = 623–644
 | title = A millennium project: constructing small groups
 | url = https://www.math.auckland.ac.nz/~obrien/research/2000.pdf
 | volume = 12
 | year = 2002}}</ref> This classification is known as the Small Groups Library.  Later with Michael F. Newman and [[Michael Vaughan-Lee]] O'Brien extended the classifications of groups of order <math>p^6</math>, <math>p^7</math>, and <math>p^8</math>.  These classifications comprise the tables provided in the computer algebra systems [[SageMath]], [[GAP (computer algebra system)|GAP]], and [[Magma (computer algebra system)|Magma]].

For a 20-year span from the mid-1990s, O'Brien led the
so-called Matrix Group Recognition Project whose primary objective is to 
solve the following problem: given a list of invertible matrices over a finite field, determine the [[composition series]] of the group.<ref>
[https://www.birs.ca/workshops/2014/14w5031/report14w5031.pdf 2014 BIRS Workshop: Algorithms for Linear Groups].  Organizers Jon F. Carlson, Bettina Eick, Alexander Hulpke, Eamonn O’Brien.</ref><ref>[https://publications.mfo.de/handle/mfo/3252 2011 MFO Workshop: Computational Group Theory]. Organizers: Bettina Eick, Gerhard Hiss, Derek Holt, Eamonn O'Brien.</ref>
Implementations of algorithms that realize the goals of this project form the bedrock of matrix group computations in the computer 
algebra system [[Magma (computer algebra system)|Magma]].
 
O'Brien's collaborations include resolution of several conjectures include the Ore conjecture, according to which all elements of non-abelian [[finite simple group]]s are [[commutator]]s.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Malle | first = Gunter
 | issue = 361
 | journal = [[Astérisque]]
 | mr = 3289286
 | article-number = Exp. No. 1069 | pages = ix, 325–348
 | title = The proof of Ore's conjecture (after Ellers-Gordeev and Liebeck-O'Brien-Shalev-Tiep)
 | url = https://www.mathematik.uni-kl.de/~malle/download/oreNov.pdf
 | year = 2014}}</ref>

==Awards==

* 2024 [[Humboldt Research Award|Alexander von Humboldt Foundation Research Award]]
* 2021 [https://nzmathsoc.org.nz/?awards New Zealand Mathematical Society Kalman Prize]

* 2020 [[Hector Medal]], [[Royal Society of New Zealand]].<ref>[https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/what-we-do/medals-and-awards/research-honours/2020-research-honours-aotearoa/2020-hector-medal/ Royal Society of New Zealand]</ref>

* 1995 [[Humboldt Fellow]]<ref>[https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/en/apply/sponsorship-programmes/humboldt-research-fellowship Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]</ref>
